November 14, 2024 Faculty Senate Meeting
Context (from JCODL 2022-2023 final report): “Several years ago (circa 2013), URI adopted definitions of online and blended learning (Face to face [< 25% online], Blended [25-75% online], and Online [75-100% online]), with the implicit, but unstated, assumption that the online portion was asynchronous. The COVID era of remote instruction gave rise to additional approaches to remote instruction and the need to reflect all available modality options and to provide clear, comprehensible and accessible definitions and descriptions for the benefit of faculty and students.”
Existing Language:
https://web.uri.edu/registration-records/faculty-staff-advisors/class-scheduling-process/.
“In-person (I): A course with no more than 24.9% of instruction delivered online. All courses are assumed to be in-person unless otherwise approved by Faculty Senate.
Blended (B): A course delivered 25%-74.9% online.
Online (O): A course delivered at least 75% online. Course must be approved as online by Faculty Senate to be scheduled as such.”
Proposed Language:

(To be inserted into Chapter 8 of the University Manual, “Academic Regulations.”)
“8.30.30 Course Modality
In-person: All instruction occurs in a specified physical location and on specified days/times.
In-person and online asynchronous: Instruction combines both in-person meetings on specified days/times and online asynchronous instruction. The schedule of instruction and the weekly time commitment to online asynchronous instruction are clear to students in the syllabus on the first day of class.
Online synchronous: All instruction occurs online at specified days/times.
Online synchronous and asynchronous: All instruction occurs online in a combination of synchronous meetings on specified days/times and asynchronous instruction. The schedule of instruction and the weekly time commitment to online asynchronous instruction are clear to students in the syllabus.
Online asynchronous: All instruction occurs online with no synchronous meetings required at specified days/times (outside of optional online office hours/meetings). The weekly time commitment to online asynchronous instruction is clear to students in the syllabus.”

HLT 602 | Integrative Learning Experience (3 crs.) This course serves as the required integrative learning experience (ILE) for MPH students, also called the Capstone Project.
The Capstone Project represents the student’s culminating experience in synthesizing, integrating, and applying the skills acquired throughout the MPH program.
This course and Capstone Project include a demonstration of competency related to leadership and professionalism and demonstrate a synthesis of foundational competencies through an individual project that addresses a public health need.

Students must complete a “high quality” written product as their Capstone Project.
